scope: Short native REST document encoder microprofile, not HTTP, consumer, RSS or official-emulator performance qualification
hypothesis: Serializing a complete typed map before replacing it with recursively normalized children serializes nested descendants repeatedly and retains unnecessary temporary JSON allocations
input: One synthetic document with 16 nested map values around a 65536-byte ASCII string, plus null, timestamp and nonfinite-double siblings; below the supported document depth and size limits
measurement: Release test process; reuse immutable typed input, construct and drop normalized JSON each iteration, black-box output. Preserve time and output SHA-256 before and after on the same host with identical test code
verification: Existing official-fixture REST read-options and document-map replay, all typed normalization unit tests and identical canonical output; every seven-job and platform check before merge
decision: Only remove demonstrated redundant serialization. No cache, workload, protocol, durability, memory-limit or acceptance-threshold changes. A microprofile speedup alone is not a full-service improvement claim.
